name: The Signing Oak

location.address: Snow Hill, Windsor Great Park, near Battle Bourne (south-west corner of the wood), Windsor SL4

access: Free. Windsor Great Park is open daily from dawn to dusk, and the Tree Register records this oak as open access on Crown Estate land. Keep out of areas the park map marks as private.
transport: Windsor & Eton Central or Windsor & Eton Riverside station, then roughly 4 km on foot along the Long Walk to Snow Hill, about an hour. The oak is roughly 500 m west-north-west of the Copper Horse statue. Park car parks are an alternative.
story:
There are two of this oak. One stands in open parkland on the edge of a wood near Snow Hill, in Windsor Great Park. The other is bronze, a replica made from scans of the living tree, and it stands in The Gallery Cafe at the Savill Garden visitor centre.

The living one was 9.55 metres round when the Tree Register recorded it in 2008, a trunk about three metres across. Windsor Great Park and the Queen's Green Canopy both call it 900 years old, and in 2022 the Canopy chose it as one of its 70 Ancient Trees. A print listing says 800. Neither figure comes with a method, so read the age as an estimate, somewhere in the twelfth or early thirteenth century for its first leaves.

The name comes from 1972. By the account attached to it, the Crown Estate Commissioners and the Nature Conservancy Council signed a Statement of Intent under its branches, recognising the park as a conservation area. That is the story the tree is known by. The Tree Register names the oak without describing the day.

It takes some reaching, about an hour on foot from Windsor down the Long Walk to Snow Hill, and then roughly 500 metres west-north-west of the Copper Horse statue. If you go, tell us how it is looking.
how_to_recognise: You can recognise it by the trunk, 9.55 metres round in 2008 and about three metres across. It stands in open parkland at the south-west corner of the wood north of Snow Hill, near Battle Bourne.

name: The Pin Oak, Canadian Memorial Avenue

location.address: Canadian Memorial Avenue, Valley Gardens, Windsor Great Park, Egham TW20

access: Free to walk into. The Tree Register records public open access on Crown Estate land in the Valley Gardens, Windsor Great Park. Car parking in the Valley Gardens is charged.
how_to_recognise: You can recognise it by its height, the tallest of the oaks along the south side of Canadian Memorial Avenue, mid-way along: 30.6 metres high and 283 centimetres round, about 90 across.
story:
The tallest pin oak in Britain and Ireland is only 90 centimetres across. The Tree Register lists this one as the height champion for its species, in those islands and in England and Surrey as well, at 30.6 metres when it was measured in 2021. Its height is about 34 times its width, a slender build for a champion.

It is not an ancient tree and nothing here pretends it is. Pin oaks come from eastern North America, and this one is one of a planted row along Canadian Memorial Avenue in the Valley Gardens, on the southern side of Windsor Great Park. We have not established when the avenue went in, so the tree's age stays open. If you know it, tell us.

The register entry is the single source for all of this, and it records the girth as 283 centimetres, Crown Estate ownership and public access. An iNaturalist record from August 2026 falls within range of the spot, though nobody has checked that it shows this particular oak.

The pin is good to about ten metres at best on an avenue of similar trees, which is why the way to find it is to look up. Go in late October, when pin oaks turn dark red.
transport: Virginia Water station is about 3 km to the south-east in a straight line, further on foot. By car, use the charged Valley Gardens car parks.

best_time.label: late October into November, when the leaves turn dark red to russet
